chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Bassam al-Sayrāfī, from Abū Ja'far (peace be upon him).
Regarding the 'ill camels (al-jallāmah), he said: 'Their meat is not to be eaten, nor are they to be ridden, for forty days.'

key_terms.الْإِبِلِ الْجَلَّالَةِ: Camels suffering from 'ill (a condition often associated with mating or illness)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating and riding camels suffering from 'ill (jallāh)?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith specifies the ruling for *al-Jallalah*—animals whose meat is prohibited due to consuming impure substances. The forty-day prohibition on eating their meat and riding them serves to purify the animal’s body, ensuring that the byproducts of their diet are expelled before consumption or use.
